strategy: read-only upstream comparison followed by narrow semantic patches; no whole-tree merge, rebase, or cherry-pick

upstream.semantic: isolate MCP OAuth credentials by execution environment
restrict hosted MCP session credentials to local environments
expose legacy shell_command only for one local environment

adaptation.environment_contract: Hepta experimental_environment values are treated as local only when absent or exactly local; every other selector is executor-owned
adaptation.oauth_key_contract: local credentials retain legacy names unless a reserved prefix requires local escaping; executor credentials use an environment-and-server encoded namespace
adaptation.fallback_store_contract: legacy host entries remain readable only by host lookups; executor lookups require an executor-owned marker and exact scoped identity
adaptation.host_auth_contract: Codex Apps session auth is never injected into executor-owned MCP transports
adaptation.shell_contract: legacy shell_command is registered only for exactly one local environment; remote and multi-environment turns must use environment-aware execution
adaptation.reserved_name_contract: an unnamespaced dynamic tool cannot reclaim the host shell_command name

authority_boundaries: no change to Hepta authenticated preference authority
no change to approval or permission authority
no change to mutation journal or release gates
no credential migration across host and executor ownership
no deployment or live configuration mutation
verification: cargo check -p codex-mcp -p codex-cli -p codex-core: passed with pre-existing dead-code warnings
cargo check -p codex-tools -p codex-core: passed with pre-existing dead-code warnings
scoped just fix attempted; codex-tools test compilation is blocked by pre-existing construction of a non-exhaustive rmcp Tool
